newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil delays open of Band B cellular bids - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil delays open of Band B cellular bids - paper.

text.p: The announcement of the consortia qualified to bid for Brazil's Band B cellular concessions will be delayed, local newspapers said on Tuesday.
Jornal do Brasil daily said a special Communications Ministry panel analysing the bids will not finish its work 45 days after the proposals were submitted as previously expected.

Communications Minister Sergio Motta had said he expected to announce May 15 to 20 which consortia had bids qualifying them to compete for the Band B concessions in 10 different areas across the country.
He also said the winners of the first two concessions, Sao Paulo city and the centre west, were expected to be announced at the end of May.
Fifteen groups have submitted bids to operate Band B concessions in nine areas.
Jornal do Brasil said Sergio Motta will travel to Portugal Thursday and will return to Brazil only on June 3.
O Globo newspaper said Motta expects the General Telecommunications Law to be approved by the full Chamber of Deputies this week, probably Thursday.
The bill, which is likely to face a vote in a lower house panel today, sets rules for the privatisation of the telecommunications sector.
